log.title: Sunwoven economy-unit sprite sheets — through the gauntlet loop to PASS (+ v2 character-sheet fidelity pass)
log.changed: New procedural sprite pipeline at sunwoven-sprites/: a Blender 5.2 headless rig (pure-Python joints, no armature; deterministic seed 20260726) renders the Citizen/villager and Pathfinder/scout economy units — idle/walk/gather (villager) and idle/walk (pathfinder), 8 compass directions, 57.5° ortho — at 512px, then post.py packs three variants: root transparent 128px cells, sprites-720p/ green 256px cells (2048² sheets), sprites-4k/ green 512px cells (4096²), each with its own manifest (anchors, fps, chroma background), plus keying masks and preview.html with a live key/unkey toggle. Three Blender 5.2 root causes fixed on the way: transform_apply(scale=True) zeroes object locations (cubes rendered ~0.5m displaced); AgX view transform desaturates warm colours (switched to Standard); material() defaulted Emission Color to gold, muddling every fabric emission (now defaults to the material's own colour). The round-1 REVISE (palette family absent, Pathfinder contract missed) was answered with a warm key/fill/rim rig, own-colour luminous fabrics, a visible turquoise sash, and a rebuilt Pathfinder (citizen-height body, narrower torso, 0.14 forward lean, 1.63m standard). FIDELITY PASS (v2 character sheets, 2026-08-06): two blind-critic rounds against the sheets. R1 REVISE (7 items — gold invisible under EEVEE no-envmap metallic void, saffron desaturated 0.41 vs sheet 0.74, gems occluded, turban smooth dome, gather stow absent, scrolls sub-pixel, lean under-spec; 3 critic claims refuted by director probes: tip-clearance metric misread, walk-hop false positive from background-inflated overlap, N-pennant sliver false). R2 PASS: gold emission 0.8/metallic 0.35 (0→1926px), saffron (0.98,0.56,0.14) sat 0.82 (reads #E2A748 golden-saffron), gems r 0.036 proud of wrap (653/489px), front-arc turban bands (reads wrapped cloth, not dome), mote route → satchel (moving centroid y465→370), scrolls r 0.018, lean 0.085 chest 8.8°/head 11.9°, ivory lifted to bible warm ivory (lit 234,209,165).
log.taught: Blind-critic loop over machine evidence (subagents have no vision tool; the project's measured-bar method applies). Round 1: REVISE — census showed 71% cool gray, zero saffron/teal, Pathfinder standard 6px above the head. Round 2: PASS — ivory 0.497/0.398, saffron 0.113/0.152, teal 0.145/0.115, gray down to 0.226/0.277; standard 24px (~36% of body height); torso 16-23px vs 22-25px (leaner, −33% at S); activity bands non-overlapping (0.437/0.682/0.758 and 0.388/0.552); gather contact anchored (node_gold 14↔0, hands 127 vs feet 128). Carried note (cosmetic): the Pathfinder renders ~10 points grayer than the villager — its forward lean tilts the torso off the key; a round 3 could lift its fill/rim. Critic models recorded: deepseek-v4-flash (opus not pinnable via delegation). FIDELITY: measured-bar discipline extended to critic claims — 3 of 10 R1 critic claims were refuted by director re-measurement (tip-clearance bar is crown-to-tip NOT tip-to-canvas-top; walk f1≈f5 overlap 0.999 was background-inflated, silhouette diff 971px; N pennant 66px ≥ range). EEVEE has no envmap: metallic >0.35 renders near-black — gold needs emission ≥0.6. Checker pitfalls paid: chin-finder must use FIRST narrow run after head max-width (last-narrow catches collarbone); pennant-sway metric must be col-centre shift not pixel-diff (wide cross-blade can't pass pixel-diff); walk-bob bar is crown span, foot travel is stride.

log.title: Economy tuning — the economy pays for the game
log.changed: Home deposits are region-aware: 700 Matter and 550 Lumen at home, with off-home values preserved at 420 Matter and 300 Lumen. The Dwelling is 55 Matter / 14 s with the existing +8 population grant. Deposit placement and every deterministic draw remain unchanged. The corrected nine-minute harness measures capability through the production API, separates no-choice stall from raw affordability delay, records denial episodes, reports Pathfinder and trained-army counts, and derives mode/seed/duration-specific output names.
log.taught: At 9:00 in economy-ceiling mode, seed 20260726, riverlands reached 42/42 population with four completed Dwellings, 12 Citizens, 13 Pathfinders, 9 Vanguards and 8 Quarrels. noChoiceStallSeconds was 0.000; raw affordability delay was 38.650 s, and all seven denial episodes had another productive action. log.title: Military roster breadth — the army finally has more than one shape in it
log.changed: BuildingKind gained .lumenSpire (90 Matter / 45 Lumen / 18 s / footprint 3.0 / 210 HP / trains Quarrel), gated behind a completed same-faction Formation Yard. UnitKind.ranged was renamed .quarrel per R1 B13 — a rename, not a second unit — and the rename boundary was checked by hand: the eleven surviving 'ranged' occurrences are all damage-type, armour-class or transport-targeting vocabulary and were correctly left alone. The Formation Yard now trains Pathfinder and Vanguard only, and its cost was corrected from 110 Matter / 40 Lumen to the design's 110 / 20. Two defects found during plan review were fixed in scope: the Vanguard's missing +8 vs siege (R1 B2), and ProductionSystem.step charging a queue item and then dropping it with no unit and no refund when no spawn slot resolved. SkirmishSimulation gained a typed BuildBlocker so a prerequisite is enforced in the simulation and not only in the HUD. The command grid became the two-page Economy / Military layout 02-BUILDING-ROSTER.md §6 specifies, and every dimmed tile now carries a visible on-screen reason. The adversary's Lumen Spire deferral closed: one Yard at tick 2400, one Spire at tick 4800, the second-Yard stand-in removed, and planArmy re-routed to pick a trainer by capability rather than by building kind — without that, the Yard losing Quarrel would have silently shrunk every wave from the second on.
log.open: The Spire does not accept Lumen drop-off — 02-BUILDING-ROSTER.md:94 says it should, but acceptsDropOff is a plain Bool and cannot express 'Lumen only'; true would make it a drop-off for all four resources. Faction modifiers absent (CP-C8). CP-C9 economy tuning is shipped: home-only yields, the 55 Matter / 14 s Dwelling, and the nine-minute evidence are recorded under Docs/QA/G3/cp-c9/. R1 §6.4's id.raw % ringSlotCount spawn rule deliberately not adopted, because the shipped ring search is already deterministic. Citizen gathering was never exercised on device this pass — both passes ran on the Core trickle. Not built from a clean clone. Three findings recorded rather than fixed: a dimmed tile's accessibility label replaces the building's identity with the reason, so a VoiceOver user cannot tell which building is gated; the multi-select panel reads '1 Pathfinders'; and the Vanguard/Quarrel read works by elongated-versus-compact, not by the vertical line 01-UNIT-ROSTER.md:156-176 claims — a vertical haft is foreshortened away by the top-down camera. The Dominion leak was re-measured (you 0 of 45 seconds, enemy 12) and stays open.

log.title: Victory and defeat — the match can end, and a stranger can win or lose it
log.changed: New Sources/Simulation/VictorySystem.swift and Sources/Domain/VictoryTypes.swift: Conquest and Dominion, judged after every other system inside the same tick so a Core that falls to this tick's combat ends the match on this tick, with Conquest tested before Dominion in Faction.allCases order because two conditions can come true together and a coin flip there would be a determinism hole. SkirmishSimulation refuses to step once MatchOutcome is set, and gained restart() to rebuild the world in place from the same seed. Dominion follows 05-RESOLUTIONS-R1.md §3 (B10) over 00-CONTENT-SPEC.md §5 where they disagree: contested DECAYS at half the fill rate rather than pausing, because a pause rule deadlocks forever if both sides keep one unit in the ring and a deadlock breaks the 'no draw state, no hard timer' promise. The hold requirement shortens 45s -> 30s (7:00) -> 20s (9:00) as a pure function of the clock. New Dominion Spire BuildingKind: neutral, pre-placed, indestructible; Building.faction became Faction? rather than gaining a .neutral case, so the compiler asks the ownership question at every site instead of a third faction flowing into every Faction.allCases loop and giving an objective a treasury. New HUD: ObjectiveRail (replacing AlertStrip, which printed one seeded sentence for an entire match) and MatchOverlay with Play Again. canCaptureDominion is its own list rather than isMilitary per B10.2.
log.observed: Played on 75898CE1 (iPad Air 13, iPadOS 26.5). VICTORY by Dominion at 3:55 with the rail at 45s/45s; VICTORY by Conquest at 15:55; DEFEAT by Conquest at 5:59 — the same wipe CP-C3 could only watch run over the corpse; DEFEAT by Resignation, named as itself rather than as a Conquest that never happened. The escalation ladder is visible on device (rail reads 0s/20s at 15:55). The world really stops: the match clock held at 0:21 across two accessibility reads seven seconds apart with the overlay up. Play Again returns the clock to 0:01, POP to 4/10 and stock to 180/160/40 with nothing left over. 49 -> 72 tests, 0 failures.
log.cost: One real defect found on the way and fixed here: the Formation Yard, Expansion Outpost and Dawn Loom had carried command tiles since CP-C1 while ConstructionPlacement.placeableKinds still listed only the three CP-G2a kinds, so beginBuildGhost bounced off the list in silence and all three tiles did nothing. The Formation Yard is the only building that trains a military unit, so the player could reach NEITHER win path; two tests now assert that everything with a price is placeable and nothing free is. The CP-C3 determinism bar is restated rather than weakened — tick 12000 is unreachable now the match ends at tick 7192, so two no-input runs must stop on the same tick with the same outcome and the same hash, which moved from a9ee7bc2faeea255 to 4645f2d24d31018c because the Spire joined the world hash and the Dominion deposits were pushed outside its footprint. Not proven: the 8-10 minute promise (no observed match landed in it), the contest rule in play (the adversary never enters the ring), and CP-C3's camera jump remains unexplained — CP-C4 moves the camera only on restart. No -sunfoldPerf smoke, deliberately, as at CP-C3. Corrected after re-measuring: the adversary DOES enter the ring — 11 s of 45 banked incidentally by waves crossing it — so what is untested is a contest with both sides present, not the adversary's presence. The frozen-clock evidence was also re-taken properly: the accessibility tree polled at 1 Hz for 12.0 s reading 5:59 throughout, replacing a screenshot-plus-one-read pair.

log.title: Adversary v0 — somebody on the other side of the map, and the thing that closed CP-C2
log.changed: New Sources/Simulation/Adversary.swift: a deterministic schedule, not a planner. Every decision is a pure function of the tick count and the world state, with no random draws at all — the tagged 'adversary' stream is reserved and deliberately unused, so a later planner cannot silently shift these numbers. It grows an economy toward twelve citizens on a 50/25/25 gather quota, commits Formation Yards at 2:00 and 4:00, houses itself on a population-headroom rule, and dispatches rising attack waves every 90 s from 4:00, routed via the Dominion centre because there is no pathfinder. New Sources/Simulation/WorldHash.swift: the canonical FNV-1a world fingerprint R1 §6.13 specifies and which nothing had implemented. SkirmishSimulation gained stepAdversary, setStance and a worldHash accessor; -sunfoldNoAdversary freezes the opponent. 49 tests pass, up from 39.
log.taught: Two things. First, a schedule beats a planner at this stage, and the way to keep it honest is to refuse to fill the gaps: five rows of the R1 §5 wave table name units that do not exist yet, and every one was DROPPED rather than substituted, listed in Adversary.deferredFromSpec, so the wave that finally fields a Lancer is a visible change rather than a silent one. Where the schedule genuinely had to be extended it was extended by measurement and written down — a second Formation Yard because with one, wave 5 came out smaller than wave 4; four Dwellings because at three the adversary jammed at 34/34 population with 340 Matter in the bank. Second, a capture technique worth keeping: at 3x speed every tool round-trip costs about ten seconds of match time, which is how the first two device runs sailed past the fight and photographed the aftermath. What works is one run-sequence that waits on a STATE CHANGE and pauses in the same call — await-ui-element on the population label going from 'Population 4 of 10' to anything else, immediately followed by a tap on Pause. That froze the match on the tick of the first kill with no timing luck involved.
log.evidence: Docs/QA/G3/cp-c3/STATUS.md — the bars table, the measured timeline, the deferred-spec table, and a 'What is not proven' section. World hash a9ee7bc2faeea255 identical on two no-input runs at tick 12000. First wave arrives 4:27, inside the 3:30–4:30 bar. Seven landscape captures on 75898CE1-… with no player input, including 03-fight-crop.png (a health bar draining next to the thing draining it) and 05-core-life-readout.png (Civilization Core · SUNWOVEN · 303 / 600).

log.title: Combat, finally observed — CP-C2 closed on evidence, not on a green suite
log.changed: No new combat code. CP-C2 shipped the system and then refused to close, because a green build and 39 green tests are not a player watching a unit die. The close is the device pass folded into CP-C3: an adversary wave walked into the player's settlement on its own and killed everything.
log.taught: The refusal was worth what it cost. Held open for hours, CP-C2 closed the same day on three frames — first blood at 4:30, first kill at 4:33, the Core destroyed at 5:59, population 0 of 10 — with NO player input at any point. The original Docs/QA/G3/cp-c2/STATUS.md is kept unedited beneath the close, because the judgement it records is the reason the proof exists at all. The general rule this project keeps relearning: when the only available evidence is the shape of evidence that has lied before, do not close; name the checkpoint that would produce real evidence and fold the verification into it.
log.evidence: Docs/QA/G3/cp-c2/STATUS.md (closed header over the untouched original) pointing at Docs/QA/G3/cp-c3/03-fight-crop.png, 05-core-life-readout.png and 07-player-wiped-pop-zero.png.

log.title: Combat core — built, tested, and deliberately NOT closed (closed later the same day as CP-C2′)
log.changed: New Sources/Simulation/CombatSystem.swift and Sources/Domain/CombatTypes.swift: armour-class damage with a minimum floor, integer-tick cooldowns on the fixed 20 Hz step, deterministic target acquisition tie-broken by EntityID, melee pathing into range, death that frees population, building destruction that cancels a production queue with a full refund. No randomness added, so no new tagged stream and no shift to any existing subsystem's numbers. Tapping a hostile with military units selected issues an attack order through the existing SelectionModel path. 39 tests pass, up from 31.
log.taught: The verification boundary, and it is the most useful thing in this entry. Combat compiles green, 39 tests pass, and the build installs and renders on the iPad — and none of that is a player watching a unit die. No fight can be staged, because the only hostiles are Gravemark's and Gravemark has no AI: nothing ever comes at you, so two hostile units never meet. This project has twice been misled by exactly this shape of evidence — a 10/10 test pass that never executed, and three sessions of green builds while a third of the map rendered magenta. So CP-C2 is committed and explicitly left open. Verification folds into CP-C3 adversary, where hostile units arrive on their own.
log.evidence: Docs/QA/G3/cp-c2/STATUS.md states exactly what is and is not proven. Build log build-agents/combat.log:1328. Landscape capture of the combat build running.
log.verdict: SHIPPED — closed as CP-C2′, see the entry above

log.title: Production — the game can now make a unit
log.changed: New Sources/Simulation/ProductionSystem.swift: per-building FIFO queue, cost charged on enqueue, progress counted in integer ticks on the fixed 20 Hz step, deterministic ring spawn resolved through WorldMap, 100%/75% cancel refund split. Queued units reserve population so the cap cannot be overshot by queueing. CommandGrid became selection-aware — a production building offers what it trains with a live cost badge, a Citizen offers the build menu — and every unavailable tile now states its own reason instead of being silently dark. Formation Yard, Expansion Outpost and Dawn Loom got build tiles. Population cap 8 to 10, Dwelling grant 4 to 8.
log.taught: Three things existed in the domain that nothing could reach. BuildingKind.trains declared what every building makes and no code read it. SkirmishTuning.maxQueueLength and cancelRefundFraction were both dead. Formation Yard, Expansion Outpost and Dawn Loom were BuildingKind cases with no build tile, and because Dawn Loom gates the Voyager age, the second age was unreachable in a shipped build. A declared-but-unwired constant is worse than a missing one: it reads as done in the source and is invisible on device. The dimmed-tile-with-a-reason pattern is the fix that generalises — the refusal on device reads "Citizen. Needs 4.11 Provisions.", an exact live number, so the player is never guessing why a button is dark.
log.evidence: Docs/QA/G3/cp-c1/ — 6 landscape captures: Core selected with Train tile, pop 4/10 to 5/10 to 7/10 across three queued Citizens, all three spawned, the refusal tile, and the six-entry Citizen build menu.

log.title: Cross-region traversal — the structural gap the critic found
log.changed: MovementSystem no longer clamps a land unit to the region it spawned in. Unit.region becomes a derived label rather than a movement constraint. Land is land; water still needs a boat. BoardingSystem widened so military units can ride a transport, and disembark restores the derived region. Two new determinism tests prove a land unit walks from the home region into the Dominion over continuous ground, and still cannot cross void water.
log.taught: This was not on any plan. The content-spec critic found it by compiling a probe against the real simulation rather than reading the code, and it invalidated three separate designs at once: Conquest needs you to reach the enemy base, Dominion needs you to hold remote nodes, and the Aether gate needs you to reach it. All three were specified against a simulation that physically could not deliver a unit to another region. The lesson is about the review method, not the bug — a critic who runs the code finds things a critic who reads it cannot.
log.evidence: Tests/DeterminismTests.swift — two new tests, part of the 31 passing under `swift test`.

log.title: Camera navigation — the minimap was a picture
log.changed: Minimap tap-to-jump and drag-to-scrub. Face north, Go to Core and Expand map wired to real actions. Place marker is dimmed and labelled rather than left as a live-looking tile for a feature that does not exist.
log.taught: Found by playing, not by reading. The minimap had no gesture recogniser of any kind and its four tool tiles had no actions, so drag-pan was the only way to move the camera on a map that takes ten seconds to cross. Nothing in the code was broken — the code was absent, and the HUD looked complete enough that four separate reviews had walked past it. An honest dimmed tile beats a dead live one.
log.evidence: Docs/QA/G2/cp-g2b-nav/ — camera panned to the map rim, then one tap on Go to Core returns to the Core.

log.title: Pose caching — the one authorised perf change
log.changed: EntityPresenter caches the seven per-unit findEntity(named:) limb lookups at spawn instead of walking the RealityKit entity hierarchy every frame for every unit.
log.taught: Directive 2 demoted performance to a guardrail and named this the single exception, because it is invisible, zero-visual-risk and buys headroom for the larger unit counts a bigger roster implies. Timeboxed to one checkpoint and closed in one. Recording it here so no later agent reopens it as a perf programme.
log.evidence: Compiles green; 31 tests pass. No perf claim is made — none was measured, and per BC-02 none was required.

log.title: Content spec critique — REVISE, and the finding that reordered the plan
log.changed: Nothing in the game. A fresh critic on claude-opus-5-thinking-max reviewed the five Docs/Design files against the real code and compiled two throwaway probes — an economy probe running the real SkirmishSimulation at 20 Hz, and a combat probe implementing the spec's own damage model — so every number in the review was measured rather than estimated.
log.taught: The largest finding was not a balance number. Unit.region is assigned at spawn and never updated, while MovementSystem clamps every land unit to its own region — so no unit has ever been able to leave the region it spawned in. A citizen ordered to the Dominion moved 21.7 m of an 816 m budget over continuous dry land and stopped at the seam. Conquest, Dominion and the Aether age gate were all unreachable for that one reason, and three serial checkpoints would each have passed their own bar before anyone noticed. I verified it myself before acting on it. Beyond that: the damage formula as written gave every archer the siege unit's +45 vs building; two files disagreed about the armour class of four of nine units in a way that inverted five matchups; the home fragment was 342 Matter short of its own building list; real gather income measured 39-59% of the book rate the costs were priced against; and three Warding Posts left a Bastion Walker at 190 of 190 HP because a damage bonus cannot answer a range deficit.
log.next: Traversal shipped as CP-G3a2, then re-author the spec against 05-RESOLUTIONS-R1 and run a second critic round before any roster content is built.

log.title: Content design specification + bar changes BC-01 and BC-02
log.changed: Authored Docs/Design/ — 00-CONTENT-SPEC (principles, two tiers, faction split, victory), 01-UNIT-ROSTER (nine unit kinds, counter triangle, full stat and time-to-kill tables), 02-BUILDING-ROSTER (fourteen buildings, each unlocking something concrete, production model, two-page command grid), 03-COMBAT-MODEL (damage formula, armour classes, tick resolution, no RNG in combat at all), 04-IMPLEMENTATION-ORDER (nine checkpoints ranked by player-visible impact). Recorded the human's bar change from Age of Empires IV to Age of Empires II: The Rise of Rome in space as BC-01, and the demotion of performance to a guardrail as BC-02, both in 00-PLAN.md with old and new side by side.
log.taught: Writing the roster forced the arithmetic, and the arithmetic found the real state of the game: the implementation order I first drafted started with combat, and playing the build showed production is missing too — which is more basic. The order was rewritten before any of it was built.
log.next: Fresh critic on claude-opus-5-thinking-max reviews the spec before any roster content is implemented.

log.title: Construction — primary defect closed on device
log.changed: Ported the r2 worktree's fixes into the main tree by hand rather than merging, because the same files carry three other agents' in-flight work. The ghost now clears on a successful placement, camera gestures are re-enabled immediately after, refunds print exact fractions (+52.5 rather than 53), boarding and aboard citizens are excluded from builder assignment, builders per site are capped at four with diminishing returns, and a tap on an incomplete friendly foundation assigns builders to it.
log.taught: Two things. First, the fix is real and photographed: place a Farm and the ghost is gone, the camera works, the panel reads +52.5 Matter. Second, and more important — the previous entry's claim that ConstructionIntegrityTests ran 10 of 10 is NOT TRUE. That worktree's own IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md records that xcodebuild test was hook-blocked there, so no test executed. In this environment xcodebuild test runs but the app-hosted bundle dies at bootstrap because the host needs ~55 s to build its scene. No test in this repository has ever actually executed. P14 is in flight to fix that.
log.next: CP-G2a-prime after P14: audio, Reduced Motion, the full placement-state matrix, Matter Extractor and Dwelling completion.

log.title: Construction — Farm, Matter Extractor, Dwelling
log.changed: Command tiles with cost and purpose copy, full-footprint placement legality, a drag ghost, cost on commit, citizens constructing with linear multi-builder progress, cancellation refund, and a completion cue.
log.taught: An independent read-only review returned REVISE on a single defect the builder had not seen: after a successful placement the ghost stays on the new foundation, which immediately makes that footprint illegal, so the flow ends on a red BLOCKED state. A separate critic found in minutes what the builder had looked straight through.
log.next: Fix the post-place ghost state before anything else. Do not begin CP-G2b.

log.title: AoE land cut by void water
log.changed: Three map layouts — riverlands, basin, fjords — built from an authored land field with carved void bodies instead of unions of discs. The minimap contours the field; causeway decks span only the wet stretch. Land coverage 75.8 / 79.4 / 77.6 percent.
log.taught: Land coverage hit its target and the frame lost its art direction. Measured after the fact, void fell to 11% and then to 2.5% after the sparse retune, against concept 01's 53%, and the black point rose from 0.002 to 0.102 — the frame now contains no true blacks. The checkpoint passed because the measurement had quietly become land coverage instead of the concept comparison every checkpoint from CP-06 to CP-08 had used.
log.next: Piece P1 — restore void contrast at the play camera without giving up the continent.

proof.play: Captured on iPadOS 26.5, all three layouts

log.title: Contiguous land maps
log.changed: Overlapping plates replaced the separate land-blob pair; coastal docks; the opening camera moved onto interior land.
log.taught: The minimap still read as discs, which is what sent the work on to CP-14.

log.title: Mostly-land maps, neutral terrain, visual leftovers
log.changed: Void-heavy composition inverted to mostly land; a shared neutral land palette so fragments are never colour-coded by civilization; the Core plaza rosette, the pier lattice, stronger rim reach, and speed controls wired to the clock.
log.taught: Faction identity belongs on units, buildings, HUD and Core livery — not on the ground.

log.title: Transport and pier
log.changed: Removed the dark spar that read as a slab bolted to the docked transport — it was the unwoven causeway field sharing the transport's dock point — and added concept 01's gold lattice pier at the rim dock.
log.taught: This frame is still the closest the project has come to concept 01: 41.5% void, a 0.002 black point, the nebula and the gas giant in shot. It is the reference for what P1 has to get back to.

log.title: HUD parity
log.changed: Top-bar centre emblem and speed cluster, an alert strip, pinned group slots, selection portraits with life meters, and minimap silhouettes drawn from the real rim outline rather than ellipses.
log.taught: Four of concept 01's five chrome surfaces now match. The group slots are still chrome only, and the alert strip shipped with a seed cue that has never cleared since.

proof.play: Captured on iPadOS 26.5, with and without a selection

log.title: Rim, deposits and plant mass
log.changed: Pale crystalline rim spurs, larger lumen clusters, and tree-scale branching crowns where every prop had previously been a medium spiky clump.
log.taught: A new prop class was not enough — the canopy pass jammed against a scatter list already packed at 1.3 metres and almost nothing placed. Scatter density is capped by site spacing, not by candidate count.

log.title: The void
log.changed: Nebula wash, the celestial body actually inside the frustum, and drifting debris. Void floor luma 0.006 to 0.036 against the concept's 0.032; soft-void fraction 0.023 to 0.362 against 0.338.
log.taught: The celestial body was never missing — it was outside the frustum. Orthographic sky cards clip hard at about ±38.7 at default zoom, so anything authored beyond that simply is not in the frame.

log.title: The Core pavilion
log.changed: The closed dark dome became concept 01's tented pavilion. Canopy-to-ground luminance 0.57 to 1.13 against the concept's 1.15; Core box median 0.162 to 0.391 against 0.394; cold shadow 0.207 to 0.029.
log.taught: Two thirds of the fix was geometry, not albedo. Flattening the canopy droop from 36 to 20 degrees under a 52-degree key moved the ratio further than every albedo change put together. A surface's value is mostly a question of what it points at.

log.title: Density and palette
log.changed: 146 plantings against the concept's 132; bare-ground hue 42.2 to 32.7 degrees against the concept's 33.0; the periodic pit lattice removed from the sand.
log.taught: The 9-degree hue error was entirely in green, and it was on every lit surface at once including a near-white hull — so it was in the light, not the albedo. Rotating hue toward red costs exposure, because green carries 71% of luminance, and had to be repaid with exposureScale.

log.title: HUD chrome
log.changed: A live Canvas minimap drawn from WorldMap rather than a baked image, with the camera footprint as a yaw-rotated quad; a fixed 3×3 command grid where an inapplicable command dims in place rather than disappearing.
log.taught: A Spacer inside a SwiftUI column with no width of its own makes the whole column greedy — the minimap panel stretched the length of the frame instead of sitting in its corner.

proof.play: Captured on iPadOS 26.5, reticle verified under a real camera pan

log.title: Terrain relief
log.changed: Relief amplitude raised across the block and a TerrainSurface contract added so units, props, deposits and decals sit on the height field instead of on a datum plane.
log.taught: The terrain had been flat to hide a missing contract — groundHeight had exactly two callers, both inside the mesh factory, so nothing else in the project knew where the ground was. Also: a height-field grid sits above the function it samples, which is why the first render lost the gold seam network.

log.title: Make the light read
log.changed: Sunlit regolith 0.540 to 0.397 linear, landing exactly on concept 01. Frame over the bloom threshold 8.34% to 0.56%. Stars became soft points with a steepest single-pixel step of 0.12 instead of 0.62.
log.taught: Three defects that had been logged separately across two sessions were one number. Measuring the frame against the concept found it in one pass and turned the fix into arithmetic — the predicted regolith median was 0.397 and the render landed on 0.397. Measure the frame before theorising about the renderer.

log.title: Kill the magenta
log.changed: Fragment meshes tag faces with per-layer material indices but were being handed a single-element material array, so every face with index 1 or above resolved to no material. Placeholder-magenta pixels: 64,490 to 0.
log.taught: The material arrays are now built with allCases.map over the layer enums, so the array index is the emitted material index by construction rather than by a hand-kept parallel list that happens to be the right length today.

log.title: Green tree and honest baseline
log.changed: Restored a compiling tree carrying three independent mid-flight breaks in three files, each hidden behind the last, left by parallel agents that never re-verified together. Added build-agents/ to .gitignore, dropping git status from 35,602 lines to 21.
log.taught: A green build proves nothing about the frame. Three sessions of visual work had compiled cleanly while a third of the map rendered magenta, because no session had ever rendered the code. Every checkpoint since ends with an installed build and a full-resolution capture, or it does not close.

proof.play: First rendered frame of this codebase, iPadOS 26.5

simLease.warning: Pass the iPad UDID 75898CE1-A691-4973-817A-973D4249A38F explicitly on every call; another project's iPhone (CD369CF5) may also be booted and must never be touched. argent's screenshot-after-gesture ignores the rotation parameter and returns a portrait-oriented frame of a landscape app — pass rotation LandscapeLeft on a standalone screenshot call when orientation matters. Confirmed again at CP-C4 close: rotate Portrait then LandscapeLeft after launch, and wait >= 12 s before judging a frame.
